title: Rabbi Zutra
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Berakhot 13b in a dispute with Rabbi Yoshiyah concerning the reading of the Shema. The Gaon Shir, in Kerem Chemed, vol. 7, p. 262, wishes to say that this is not a personal name but refers to Rabbi Yehudah Nesia, who was “junior” relative to Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, his grandfather. Hyman rejects this, arguing that this Rabbi Zutra and Rabbi Yoshiyah were both Babylonian Tannaim who lived in Rabbi’s time, and therefore they are mentioned in a baraita.

notes.text: שי״ר is read as Shlomo Yehudah Rapoport. The supplied Kerem Chemed marker ש״ן remains literal rather than an unverified year 7 conversion; page 262 is preserved. The volume question keeps the notice held. Hyman owns the disagreement about the name and Babylonian Tanna identification.

The earlier note records the uncertainty before the printed volume was located. Hyman’s printed text (vol. I, p. 382) has ש״ז where the supplied Hebrew has ש״ן. Shlomo Yehudah Rapoport discusses his proposal in Kerem Chemed, vol. 7 (1843), pp. 262–263, including alternate ways to understand the name. In the Berakhot 13b text consulted, the Shema dispute names Rav Zutra and Rabbi Yoshiyah. The identification proposed by Rapoport and the dating argued by Hyman remain their respective readings.
